lado_card.rot: The tool for the practice sessions
lado_card.texto: Open-source simulator from Google DeepMind and the official collection of robot models. All practice sessions run on CPU; tested with mujoco 3.16.0 and Menagerie 62ab00f on 10/19/2026.

inicio.kicker: FTH — Humanoid Technology Training · course 0 of 5 · 8 lessons
inicio.titulo: The humanoid's body: from actuator to simulation model
inicio.lead: Before you teach a humanoid to walk, you need to know what it is made of. In eight lessons you tell demo from production, open the Unitree G1 in MuJoCo, read joints, actuators, and sensors straight from the file, measure torque, balance, and runtime, and build the spec sheet. All on CPU, no robot.
inicio.capa_alt: Industrial humanoid robot standing in a dark lab, strapped to a safety gantry, with the title The humanoid's body.
inicio.aulas_sub: From the October 2026 market to the spec sheet: what is actually shipping, how the body is described in an MJCF, joints, actuators, sensors, balance, compute, and battery.

itens: People who code in Python, have seen ROS 2 (or took the robot course), and want to work with humanoids.
People without a humanoid: the practice sessions run in MuJoCo, on CPU, in seconds. No GPU needed.
People who need to read a robot's spec sheet and separate what is in the file from what is in the marketing.

blocos.t: What you'll be able to do
itens: Classify a humanoid as demo, pilot, or production, with source and date.
Open any humanoid from the MuJoCo Menagerie and read joints, limits, actuators, and sensors.
Measure torque, foot load, and balance margin with a script, with output you can check.
Work out runtime and loop time, and build the spec sheet comparing two models.
